Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjeev Narula
 Order

Petitioner No. 1 (husband) and Petitioners No. 2 to 4 (in-laws of Respondent No. 2) have filed the present petition seeking quashing of FIR No. 401/2025 dated 22nd September, 2025, registered at P.S. Paschim Vihar West, Delhi under Sections 498A, 406, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, as well as all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. At present, the matter is at the stage of investigation.
Counsel for the Petitioners submits that the entire case of the prosecution rests on the complaint of Respondent No. 2, which is completely misconceived and false.
It is submitted that Respondent No. 2 married Petitioner No. 1 on 19th March, 2023 and resided in India for only about one month, out of which 15 days were spent at her parental home.
Respondent No. 2 left for Denmark on 21st April, 2023, and Petitioner No. 1 later joined her in November, 2023.
This is a digitally signed order.

It is, therefore, argued that the allegations in the FIR, particularly pertaining to July 2023, are false as Respondent No. 2 was not residing with any of the Petitioners at that time.

sentences.text: On the other hand, counsel for Respondent No. 2 submits that Respondent No. 2 was in India at the relevant time and disputes the factual assertions of the Petitioners.
It is further submitted that Petitioner No. 1 also has a criminal case pending against him in Denmark, and all allegations levelled in the FIR are genuine.

5. Since these are disputed questions of fact and the matter is still under investigation, this Court is of the view that the Investigating Officer will have to verify the factual position, investigate to determine whether any of the Petitioners is culpable of any offence alleged.
At this stage, no coercive action is contemplated, as confirmed by Mr. Hemant Mehla, APP for the State, on instructions from the Investigating Officer present.
6. In view of the above, the rights and contentions of the Petitioners are reserved.
They shall be at liberty to take recourse to appropriate remedies in accordance with law should the investigation culminate in any action adverse to them.
The Petitioners are also at liberty to furnish all relevant documents to the Investigating Officer, who shall examine the same in accordance with law.
7. The present petition stands disposed of in the above terms.
9. Pending application(s) also stands disposed of.
SANJEEV NARULA, J DECEMBER 5, 2025/MK
